result.rationale: In sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse parses against minimumTokenResponseSchema, which strips unknown fields by default (dropping the new expiry) and then injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` if absent. The O365 caller then spreads this data into o365AuthCredentials and persists it via prisma.credential.update, overwriting the real refresh token with the placeholder and losing the refreshed expiry. Verifiable in the diff (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts and office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts changes).

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts. Looking at lines 23-25, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the function uses minimumTokenResponseSchema which only validates access_token exists, then unconditionally sets `refresh_token: 'refresh_token'` (a fake placeholder) if no refresh_token is present. In Office365CalendarService.ts line 264, the code spreads tokenResponse.data into o365AuthCredentials. The minimumTokenResponseSchema doesn't capture expires_in/expiry_date properly (the schema definition on lines 7-10 uses invalid z.string().toString() as keys which won't work as intended), and the fake refresh_token will overwrite the real one. This means in sync mode, the credential will have a fake refresh_token and potentially missing/incorrect expiry data, causing subsequent refreshes to fail.
